cells.tense: The pen is in your hand right now and the mixing is steady.
cells.act: make the fair call about a feeling, yourself
cells.ask: Take a feeling from this week you haven't sorted — weigh it by yourself, what it's owed and what it isn't, and don't put it up for a vote.
cells.core:
You have a working sense of what to keep at the table and what to clear, and you don't labor over it. Something goes stale and you turn it under; something still feeds and it stays. The meal comes out even because you kept adjusting while it cooked.

So when a feeling of your own has been sitting too long, take it in hand and weigh it plainly. What does it actually cost, what does it give, whose side of the scale does it fall on. Not a verdict, not a bill — a fair call from the one who knows the kitchen. Fairness runs when you don't second-guess it.

Start with one feeling from this week you haven't weighed. Decide what it's owed, and stop there. The judgment is a hand on the scale, not a court.

cells.tense: You'll have the whole release done and the new growth plotted before any of it has arrived.
cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: Pick one person in a shared thing and ask what being there feels like to them right now. Stay with whatever comes back — fix nothing, plan nothing, add nothing.
cells.core:
At the table, the next round of rescuing is already underway. You can feel the kitchen's future in your hands before anyone has spoken — who needs which ending, what has to be cleared by when, what gets planted after. It reads as care from your side. From the other side it reads as control, and people hand you only what's already finished.

The adjusting isn't the problem; the speed is. Sit inside one thing instead of reaching into it. Ask what it feels like to them and stay there — no fixing, no plan for what it means. What you hear belongs to them, not to you. The next ending you make belongs to the room that has actually reached it, and there will be fewer. Fewer, and truer.

cells.tense: A door closed behind you and you're still standing where it used to be.
cells.act: feed the drive a little at a time
cells.ask: Pick the smallest wanted thing in your week — a walk, a page, the start of something — and move on it before you feel steady.
cells.core:
The table is set and you're not at it. The adjusting has gone quiet in you: no reading of what to add, no reading of what to release, just a room kept the way it was. What ended has stopped being yours to end, and you've kept its slot warm without noticing you're no longer in it.

Direction comes before feeling here. Move on one small wanted thing today — a walk, a page, a start — without waiting to feel ready. Feed the fire a little and warmth comes back to the room. Purpose runs ahead of mood, not behind it; the drive wasn't gone, only unfed.

One thing, without needing to feel settled first. Tomorrow can hold the next one.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you have been writing in the whole time.
cells.act: set a boundary and hold it
cells.ask: In one shared thing, mark a line you won't cross back over — a limit about your time or your part — and keep it held without renegotiating.
cells.core:
You've been tuning this room — moving what's too much, keeping what still feeds, blending without fuss. Nobody mentions who keeps it running. It runs because someone keeps adjusting it, and the adjusting has been quiet work.

Before this was upkeep, it was you deciding. Pick one shared thing and set a boundary inside it — a line about what you'll give or where your part ends — and hold it without a vote. What you set, stays; what you don't, drifts. A boundary is the door you've been holding shut with your shoulder, written down.

One line, held for a full week. See what the room does when it has to hold itself.
